questions.q: Where did Buck live before he was stolen?
choices: On a sheep ranch outside Seattle
At Judge Miller's place in the Santa Clara Valley
At a gold miner's cabin in the far North
In a kennel behind a San Francisco saloon
questions.evidence: Buck lived at a big house in the sun-kissed Santa Clara Valley

questions.q: Why did so many men suddenly want big, strong dogs with furry coats?
choices: Dog sled racing had become a popular sport in California
The army needed dogs to guard its forts in the far North
Gold had been found in the Arctic and men were rushing north
Farmers needed strong dogs to herd their cattle through snow
questions.evidence: had found a yellow metal

questions.q: How did Buck think of himself on Judge Miller's place?
choices: As a king over everything there, humans included
As a lowly kennel-dog who had to obey the terriers
As a pampered house-dog who rarely went outdoors
As a guard dog whose only job was to watch the stables
questions.evidence: for he was king

questions.q: What kinds of dogs were Buck's father and mother?
choices: A Newfoundland father and a collie mother
A wolf father and a husky mother
A St. Bernard father and a Scotch shepherd mother
A mastiff father and a Scotch terrier mother
questions.evidence: His father, Elmo, a huge St. Bernard

questions.q: Why did Manuel, the gardener's helper, sell Buck to a stranger?
choices: The Judge had quietly told him to get rid of the dog
He was angry that Buck had bitten one of his children
A stranger threatened to hurt him unless he gave up Buck
He needed money because of his gambling in the lottery
questions.evidence: He loved to play Chinese lottery

questions.q: Where was the Judge on the night Manuel led Buck away?
choices: At a meeting of the Raisin Growers' Association
Away on a long trip by train to San Francisco
Asleep in front of the library fire at home
Out hunting in the hills with his two sons
questions.evidence: The Judge was at a meeting of the Raisin Growers' Association

questions.q: When Manuel put a rope around Buck's neck, "it was an unwonted performance." What does "unwonted" mean here?
choices: Unwanted and hated
Unusual, not what he was used to
Dangerous and likely to hurt
Practiced and rehearsed many times before
questions.evidence: it was an unwonted performance

questions.q: What did the kidnapper tell the baggageman on the train about Buck?
choices: That Buck was a show dog being sent to a contest
That Buck had fits and a dog-doctor would cure him
That Buck had been sold to a miner going to Alaska
That Buck was a stray he had found by the tracks
questions.evidence: Yep, has fits

questions.q: In the shed behind the saloon, what did the men do to Buck before leaving him for the night?
choices: Filed off his brass collar and shut him in a crate
Tied him to a post and gave him a bowl of water
Painted over his coat so the Judge could not find him
Put a muzzle on him and locked him in a back room
questions.evidence: filing the heavy brass collar from off his neck

questions.q: Each time the shed door rattled open in the night, what did Buck hope to see?
choices: The Judge, or at least the boys
Manuel coming back to set him free
A man bringing him food and water
The other dogs from the Judge's kennels
questions.evidence: expecting to see the Judge, or the boys at least

questions.q: How long did Buck go without eating or drinking in the express car?
choices: One long night
Two days and nights
Four days and nights
Almost a whole week
questions.evidence: For two days and nights Buck neither ate nor drank

questions.q: Why did the express messengers' teasing make Buck so much angrier?
choices: It hurt his dignity, and his anger grew and grew
He thought they were going to steal his food
He believed they were the men who had sold him
It reminded him of the terriers who teased Toots
questions.evidence: the more outrage to his dignity, and his anger waxed and waxed

questions.q: By the time he reached Seattle, Buck "was metamorphosed into a raging fiend." What does "metamorphosed" mean?
choices: Calmed and comforted
Tied up and carried off
Completely changed
Fed and given water
questions.evidence: he was metamorphosed into a raging fiend

questions.q: What did the four men who carried the crate do when the man in the red sweater began to open it?
choices: They held the crate steady so Buck could not tip it
They scattered and climbed on top of the wall to watch
They ran inside the house and locked the door behind them
They tossed ropes over Buck's head as he came out
questions.evidence: from safe perches on top the wall they prepared to watch

questions.q: What lesson did Buck learn from the man in the red sweater, which he never forgot?
choices: That all men are cruel and none of them can ever be trusted
That he could win any fight if he was angry enough
That he stood no chance against a man with a club
That dogs who wag their tails get the best food
questions.evidence: he stood no chance against a man with a club

questions.q: The book says Buck "was beaten" but "not broken." What does that mean?
choices: He was hurt badly, but none of his bones were broken
He lost the fight but kept his pride and spirit
He gave up and began to fawn on the man with the club
He was not hurt at all because he dodged the club
questions.evidence: He was beaten (he knew that); but he was not broken

questions.q: Who bought Buck from the man in the red sweater, and for whom?
choices: Francois, for a gold miner on the Yukon
Manuel, so he could return him to the Judge
A whaling captain, for a trip to Spitzbergen
Perrault, using money from the Canadian Government
questions.evidence: The Canadian Government would be no loser

questions.q: How did Buck come to feel about Perrault and Francois?
choices: He loved them as much as he had loved the Judge
He feared them and tried to escape at every chance
He respected them because they were fair men
He hated them for taking him away from Seattle
questions.evidence: he none the less grew honestly to respect them

questions.q: What was Dave, one of the dogs on the Narwhal, like?
choices: Gloomy, and he only wanted to be left alone
Friendly, but he stole food when no one looked
Nervous, and he howled whenever the ship rolled
Playful, and he wrestled with Curly all day
questions.evidence: all he desired was to be left alone

questions.q: At the end of the chapter, what was the strange white stuff that puzzled Buck on the deck?
choices: Salt spray from the stormy sea
Flour spilled from the ship's stores
Ashes blowing down from the ship's tall smokestack
Snow, which he was seeing for the first time
questions.evidence: for it was his first snow
